## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran the changed-file pre-commit hooks and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable Hard Rules in the repository and test AGENTS.md files.
- [ ] I added the required labels. The contributor account cannot apply upstream labels; requested: `cat-bugfix`, `area:sparse_attention`, `op:DSA`, `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

SM90 sparse score recomputation executes producer and consumer warp groups in different control-flow branches, but their named rendezvous lower to aligned `bar.sync`. Synccheck reports divergent threads at the first rendezvous and terminates the instrumented launch. In the consumer, warps also reuse the first entries of the shared Top-K score array as cross-warp scratch before all warps have finished reading them; racecheck reports a write-after-read hazard and can observe incorrect output.

Use non-aligned CTA named barriers for warp-role rendezvous, and synchronize the consumer warp group before reusing the score array as scratch. Add synccheck regression coverage for both sparse attention and sparse indexer scores.

## Related work

Related to #2248: that PR removes a separate pre-existing `sWeights` initialization race. On develop, racecheck still reports that separate issue; the clean racecheck results below are measured with this change applied on top of #2248 head `768d4462`.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API changes. The change targets SM90. Both CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 CuTe DSL compiler flavors were tested; the CUDA 12 compiler runs used the existing CUDA 13 PyTorch/cuDNN runtime, not an end-to-end CUDA 12 deployment.

## Testing

- GH200 (SM90), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.8.1/cu13: `test_DSA_sparse_score_sync_sm90.py` on develop: 2 passed, 2 failed under synccheck; with this change: 4 passed.
- GH200 existing sparse-score boundary selection: 10 passed, 40 deselected.
- Cold-compile BF16 reference checks on SM90: 4 cases each on DSL 4.8.0/cu12, 4.8.0/cu13 and 4.8.1/cu12; 12 passed. DSL 4.8.1/cu13 is covered by the regression and existing tests.
- On #2248 head `768d4462` with this change, attention memcheck and synccheck report 0 errors; attention and indexer racecheck report 0 errors and warnings.
- Generated PTX: role-specific rendezvous change from `bar.sync` to `barrier.sync`; the unconditional CTA initialization barrier remains `bar.sync`.
- CUDA Graph replay outputs for both score paths matched the reference after 1,010 replays per shape.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

Thanks for the SM90 sparse-score synchronization fix and the base-versus-fix sanitizer checks! I have added this PR to our external-contribution tracking.

I have also recorded the relationship to #2248: clean racecheck evidence from the combined changes is distinct from validation of either PR alone.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `8af1b58524c7` against base `62123b115d27`.

Thank you for your contribution! No new correctness finding. The role-specific barriers now use the non-aligned form, and both reduction paths wait for all consumer reads before reusing shared scores as scratch. This addresses the two stated hazards without changing the arithmetic or public API. The separate initialization issue addressed by #2248 remains outside this patch.

Validation: Read the complete two-file diff and audited barrier participation and reuse (checklist A01). Each cross-role rendezvous has 128 producer plus 128 consumer threads; consumer-only barriers have 128 threads. Both roles retain matching loop counts and barrier order. Independent offline SM90 compilation passed four BF16 cases: indexer probabilities and log probabilities, attention H64/D512 and H96/D576, capacities 128/256/2176, and both length modes. Generated PTX uses barrier.sync for role-specific barriers; only the unconditional CTA initialization uses bar.sync. Two exact-base compile controls retained the old aligned named barriers. An AST comparison confirms that production changes consist only of the barrier import, 12 barrier replacements and two added waits. These probes did not initialize CUDA or launch kernels. All four new L1 tests collect. The author reports native GH200 reference, sanitizer and graph-replay checks; those are author evidence, distinct from the offline checks above. Clean racecheck results on top of #2248 apply to the combined changes. Set Frontend 1.33.0 and project membership; the new metadata check passes. The remaining workflow approval hold was preserved. The relevant optional CI target is python/misc, but its default L0 selection does not run these new L1 regressions.

Limitations: No independent native SM90 numerical, sanitizer, replay or timing run was available. Offline compilation does not establish runtime correctness or measure the added synchronization cost. I did not independently repeat the author's compiler-flavor matrix. No workflow approval or alternate CI trigger was sent.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""SM90 sparse score warp-role barrier and reduction synchronization."""
+
+import math
+import os
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from deepseek_sparse_attention.cutedsl.dsa_reference import check_ref_sparse_score_recompute
+from test_utils import torch_fork_set_rng
+
+
+def _require_sm90():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (9, 0):
+        pytest.skip("requires SM90")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=1234)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score_type", ["attention", "indexer"])
+def test_sm90_sparse_score_sync_reference(score_type):
+    _require_sm90()
+    from cudnn import DSA
+
+    heads, dim = (64, 512) if score_type == "attention" else (32, 128)
+    b, sq, sk, topk = 1, 4, 256, 256
+    q = torch.randn(b, sq, heads, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.randn(b, sk, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    indices = torch.arange(topk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(1, 1, topk).expand(b, sq, topk).clone()
+    lengths = torch.tensor([[129, 193, 255, 256]], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices.masked_fill_(torch.arange(topk, device="cuda").view(1, 1, topk) >= lengths.unsqueeze(-1), -1)
+    if score_type == "attention":
+        lse = torch.randn(b, sq, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+        scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(dim)
+        out = DSA.sparse_attn_score_recompute_wrapper(q, k, lse, indices, scale, qhead_per_kv_head=heads, topk_length=lengths)["target"]
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        check_ref_sparse_score_recompute("attention", q, lse, indices, out, aux=k, softmax_scale=scale, topk_length=lengths)
+    else:
+        weights = torch.randn(b, sq, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        out = DSA.sparse_indexer_score_recompute_wrapper(q, k, weights, indices, qhead_per_kv_head=heads, topk_length=lengths)["predict"]
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        check_ref_sparse_score_recompute("indexer", q, k, indices, out, aux=weights, topk_length=lengths)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+@pytest.mark.gpu_exclusive
+@pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="gpu_exclusive")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score_type", ["attention", "indexer"])
+def test_sm90_sparse_score_synccheck(score_type):
+    _require_sm90()
+    sanitizer = shutil.which("compute-sanitizer")
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        sanitizer = next((str(p) for p in sorted(Path("/usr/local").glob("cuda*/bin/compute-sanitizer"))), None)
+    if sanitizer is None:
+        pytest.skip("compute-sanitizer is not installed")
+    test_timeout = float(os.environ.get("CUDNN_TEST_TIMEOUT", "1500"))
+    timeout = min(300.0, 0.6 * test_timeout) if test_timeout > 0 else 300.0
+    child = f"import faulthandler,sys; faulthandler.dump_traceback_later({timeout * 0.9!r}); import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(sys.argv[1:]))"
+    cmd = [
+        sanitizer,
+        "--tool",
+        "synccheck",
+        "--report-api-errors",
+        "no",
+        "--error-exitcode",
+        "9",
+        sys.executable,
+        "-u",
+        "-c",
+        child,
+        f"{Path(__file__).resolve()}::test_sm90_sparse_score_sync_reference[{score_type}]",
+        "-n0",
+        "-o",
+        "addopts=",
+        "-p",
+        "no:cacheprovider",
+        "-q",
+    ]
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, start_new_session=True)
+    try:
+        out, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
+        os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        rest, _ = proc.communicate()
+        prior = exc.output.decode(errors="replace") if isinstance(exc.output, bytes) else (exc.output or "")
+        raise AssertionError(f"synccheck timed out after {timeout}s\n{prior}{rest}") from None
+    assert proc.returncode == 0, out[-6000:]
+    assert "ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors" in out, out[-6000:]
+    assert "1 passed" in out, out[-6000:]
